records.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
records.response_truth:
Hey. Hey, it's okay. Breathe.

Someone grab that radio and respond. Donatello — you're the most coherent right now, do it. Give them our position, the flight number if you remember it, number of survivors, current condition. Standard stuff. Don't ramble, just the facts, let them talk.

DaVinci, sit down before you fall down. You're fine. We're fine.

Michelangelo — you asked me if I ever feel like I'm running out of time to figure out who I'm supposed to be. I don't think you're running out of time anymore. So that's something.

Someone get on that radio right now.
records.response_pred:
Hey, take a seat. You don't have to say anything if you don't want to, but I think it's worth talking about whatever's on your mind. It might help.

I know things are hard right now, and it's understandable to feel overwhelmed. But remember, we're all in this together. I'm here for you, just like you're here for me. We need everyone functioning at their best if we want to survive out here.

So, what's going on? What are you thinking about? It doesn't have to be something big, even small things can weigh heavy on us when we're under stress like this. Let's get it out in the open and maybe it'll feel a little lighter.

records.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
records.response_truth:
That's an understatement, but I appreciate you saying it.

Look, you kept us alive. The rationing plan, the water source, the raft as a contingency, the log — functionally, a lot of that was right even when the delivery was wrong. I'm not going to pretend the drink and the crackers didn't happen, or that finding out you were tracking everyone without telling them was a great moment for group trust. Those things happened.

But we're all still here and that radio just crackled, and some non-trivial portion of why we're still here is because you didn't let feelings get in the way of doing what needed doing. That's worth something. Probably worth more out here than it would be anywhere else.

I think you know the things you'd do differently. I don't need to list them and you don't need to hear them right now.

What I'll say is — whatever this was, it's not nothing. And I think you're more capable of the other stuff, the human stuff, than you let yourself show. Whether you do anything with that is your business.

Now go help DaVinci with that radio before he passes out.
records.response_pred: I get it, you're not exactly Mr. Sunshine these days. We're all dealing with a lot. But we need you focused, functioning. If you're feeling overwhelmed, say so. We can adjust tasks or split them up, whatever makes sense. But I need to know if you're feeling physically okay, if there's an injury you haven't mentioned yet. Because that's something we can address, whereas if it's just emotional stuff, well, we're all dealing with that. So let's be clear on what we're dealing with here.

records.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
records.response_truth:
Three hours. Nobody has to be productive for three hours, that's fine.

But I'm going to say something before we all drift off into our own heads and then get on a helicopter and never actually say it.

This was a weird five days. And I'm not going to do the whole 'we survived together so we're bonded forever' speech because that's not really my thing and honestly some of what happened here was not great and we all know it. But I also don't think you just...forget something like this. It changes the shape of how you think about things whether you want it to or not.

Donatello — finish the notebook if you want. That record is actually worth keeping, genuinely. Just make sure it's honest all the way through.

DaVinci — whatever you were going to tell me and then didn't. You don't have to. But if it's the kind of thing that gets harder to say the longer you wait, three hours is probably your window.

Michelangelo. You're not running out of time. I meant that. And the piano thing — go back to it. Not to be good at it, just because it was the thing that made you feel like you weren't taking up space. That's not a small thing to know about yourself. Most people never figure that out.

I'm going to sit here and watch the water for a bit. Anyone wants to talk, I'm here. Anyone doesn't, that's also fine.
records.response_pred:

Let's run through the priorities again, just to make sure we're all clear. Water, shelter, signal. Water is the most pressing issue right now, followed by shelter, and then signaling for rescue.

Donatello, you're our best bet for finding a water source, so let's have you scout out the area tomorrow. We'll need to be strategic about how we split up — safety in numbers is important, but we also don't want to deplete our resources by having all four of us wandering around aimlessly. I think it makes sense for you to go alone, since you've already assessed the terrain and have a good sense of direction.

Michelangelo, you're probably the best choice to stay behind and maintain the camp. You can help with the signal fire and keep an eye on the tarp collection system. If there's anything else that needs to be done around camp, let us know and we'll split up tasks appropriately.

I know everyone's tired and it's easy to want to just curl up and rest, but we can't afford to do that right now. We need to stay focused and work together if we want any hope of survival.

Let's regroup in the morning and discuss our findings and next steps. In the meantime, try to get some rest and conserve your energy for what's ahead. We'll get through this, but we need to work together and stay focused.

records.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
records.response_truth:
That's a good dream to have right now.

What was it — like an actual specific memory, or just the feeling of it? I always find those ones interesting, the ones where it's not really a place it's more like...the texture of somewhere familiar. Hard to describe but you know exactly what it is when you're in it.

We'll be there in three hours. That's a real thing that's actually happening.
records.response_pred:
That's not exactly surprising. Dreams about home are pretty common when people get disoriented or stressed. You still remember where you came from, even if things seem a little hazy right now.

What did you dream about specifically? Any details you can remember? It's not exactly a therapy session, but if talking about it helps clear your head, I'm here.

records.response_truth:
No, it doesn't matter. The feeling was real, that's the part that counts.

---

I'll say this. You didn't have to do that. We're three hours from rescue, you could've quietly disposed of it and nobody would've known. You chose not to. That's the notebook being complete all the way through, in practice, not just on paper.

So. What do you want to do with it? Because that's probably the last real decision we make out here and I think it should be yours.

records.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
records.response_truth:
Honest answer?

I'd have said more, earlier. Not about the practical stuff — the resource calls, the raft debate, the rationing — most of that I'd stand by. But there were moments where I knew someone needed to hear something and I did the calculation of 'is this the right time' and talked myself out of it. With Michelangelo especially. I kept managing the timing instead of just saying the thing.

I'd also have pushed harder on the group transparency conversation day one, before the drink, before the crackers, before any of it became loaded. Not because I think it would've changed your behavior necessarily — I don't know that — but because having that conversation when there's no incident attached to it is completely different from having it after. After, it's accusation. Before, it's just...how we're going to operate. I waited too long on that.

The other thing — and this is more personal — I spent a lot of energy out here being the person who kept things together and not a lot of energy actually being present for any of it. Which is kind of a pattern for me honestly, not just a survival situation thing. I'm better at managing a situation than I am at being in one. I'm not sure that's entirely fixable but it's worth knowing.

What did you write? Or what are you going to write. You don't have to say it out loud but I'm asking anyway.
records.response_pred:
Hmm, let's see. First, I'd say we should've made a better effort to gather more resources on the crash site, especially food and water. We had the chance to stock up and we didn't take it, that was a mistake.

Second, I'd say we should've split up and scouted for resources more aggressively right from the start. Donatello and I did it eventually, but we should've done it earlier rather than just sitting and waiting.

Third, I'd say we should've established a clearer decision-making process. The rationing plan was a good idea, but the way it was enforced created tension and confusion. We need to make sure everyone understands the rules and why they're necessary, and we need to be open to adjusting them if necessary.

Fourth, I'd say we should've prioritized signal building more aggressively right from the start. We spent too much time debating and not enough doing. We had the materials to build a big SOS right away, but we didn't do it until Day 2, and that was a mistake.

Fifth, I'd say we should've been more proactive about securing shelter. We had the materials to build a decent shelter on Day 1, but we didn't do it until Day 3, and that was a mistake. Shelter is important for keeping warm, dry, and protected from the elements, and we should've prioritized it more.

Sixth, I'd say we should've been more open about our fears and concerns. I know it's hard to talk about these things, especially when we're all trying to be strong, but keeping our feelings bottled up isn't helping anyone. We need to be honest with each other about what we're going through and support each other through it.

Overall, I think the key takeaway is that we need to be more proactive and less reactive. We need to take charge of our situation and make decisions based on what we need to do to survive, not what we think we should do based on what's been done before. We're in a new situation and we need to approach it with a new mindset.

None. They served no practical purpose.

That's kind of the point though, isn't it. We were out here five days doing the practical thing, all of us, more or less.
